doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Arriving in Chicago: the 31st Street apartment above the Royal Gardens
summary: His hip uncle found an apartment above the cabaret where King Oliver played, then they moved to Cottage Grove.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So your father and uncle were already up there in Chicago . . .

Yeah, and once they got settled and everything there – my uncle is very hip. He was well- educated [and] very hip. [He] got an apartment and everything for us. We all lived together. He had his wife come up. He and his wife – everybody – that’s the way the whole thing lined up. When we came, we came to an apartment. It was there. That was it.
Do you recall that apartment?

Oh yes. I recall the first place we moved in was an apartment on 31st Street. It was in a building. In this building on the main floor was a nightclub, which they called a cabaret. In this cabaret King Oliver’s band played, and it had the signs in the lobby of this building that we lived in. That’s where I first heard or knew about King Oliver. We could hear the music when you came in. Like when the thing was going on, we could hear the music, go to rehearsals and that stuff, because it was right on the main floor. Part of it – this nightclub place – was on the main floor of this building that we lived in, the first place we moved in. Then later on – I think after a couple of years there – we moved to a larger apartment, because some of the other parts of my family decided to come up. I think that’s when my grandmother and grandfather and all them came up. See, actually, my mother and father and that part of it came up first. Then the older people came up much later. When my grandmother and grandfather came up, we were on Cottage Grove – 2934 Cottage Grove, which was between 31st and – it was the lakefront. We could walk to the lake. Just go past the railroad tracks, which was where the Illinois Central ran, and there you were right at the lake. The tracks and everything were right on Lake Michigan, right on the lakefront.
This is where the cabaret was?
No, no. The cabaret scene was in the first place, when we first – the first place I lived there.
Where was the Royal Garden Club?
That’s it. That’s where – it was in that building. That was the Royal Gardens.
What street was that on?
31st and, I guess, Calumet.
Right. So basically you moved along 31st Street from – I think you said . . .
From New Orleans.
Yeah. From 2934 Cottage Grove . . .
No, I think it’s the other way around.
From 31st Street to Cottage Grove.
To Cottage Grove. Right.
I’m assuming that that wasn’t far. Each place . . .
No. 29 – 30 – 31. Three blocks. But, a few blocks east. Cottage Grove was a few blocks east of Calumet.
What did the few blocks east represent, in terms of . . . ?
It’s just like . . .
A bigger place?
Yeah. It was three blocks. The blocks in Chicago going from east to west are long. North to south are short.
